nodes.claim_text: [10-15] Among OORs, the low-potential aldehyde oxidation reaction (LP AOR) using Cu-based catalysts has become a sought- after anodic reaction in the hybrid EWS system duo to the ultra-low oxidation potential (∼ 0.1 VRHE).[16-23] Additionally, compared to LP AOR ǁHER system, biomass fuel cell sys- tem by integrating LP AOR with oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) can accomplish the transformation of H 2 production and biomass aldehyde upgrading from energy input to energy output.[24,25] Usually, owing to the spontaneous C ─ H bond cleavage in aldehyde in LP AOR, together with the appropriate adsorption strength of the resulting H* intermediates on Cu catalysts, favors H*-H* recombination via T afel step (H* + H* → H2) rather than Faradaic Volmer pathway (H* + OH- → H2O + e- ),[17,26] enabling anodic H2 evolution in hybrid electrolysis systems.

nodes.claim_text: Furthermore, the distribution of relaxation time (DRT) analysis based on in situ EIS data was employed to exhaustively elucidate the complicated FFOR process, which can allow the direct extraction of the timescales and resistances to distinguish different electrochemical pro- cesses without requiring a predetermined physical circuit model.[51,52] By the deconvolution of the DRT peaks, the FFOR electrochemical processes are segmented into different time constants ( τ) relevant to electron transfer between the inner layer and the reaction interface at high frequency region (10- 4<τ 1 < 10- 3 s), and interface charge transfer and inter- mediate accumulation processes at low and middle frequency regions (10- 3<τ2 < 101 s).[53] Withinτ1 range, the DRT peaks of An-CrCuxO-AC NWAs and An-CuxO-AC NWAs catalysts are very much alike, which signiﬁes that the electron transfer process at interface is not determinant factor responsible for their differences in catalytic performance (Figure 5g,h).
